text: Hey everybody. Every time I mention that
I have two master's degrees, I see a
bunch of comments that are acting as if
that's some kind of overachievement on
my part. And it is actually the exact
opposite. I was compelled to do two
master's degrees. I didn't want to do
two master's degrees. See, when I
finished my bachelor's degree at Brigham
Y Young University, I applied to a bunch
of master's programs and a bunch of PhD
programs. and I got accepted to one PhD
program at Claremont Graduate University
and then a master's at Trinity Western
University and another masters at the
University of Oxford. And I really
wanted to do the PhD program, but the
person that I applied to do the program
with left for another university in
between applying and being accepted. So
they assigned me to another uh
supervisor, not someone I had any kind
of problem with, but it wouldn't be the
project that I wanted to work on. And
also I really liked the idea of going
over and doing a master's degree at
Oxford. So uh although my wife was
already picking out uh season passes to
Disneyland, I said I really wanted to go
do the master's degree at Oxford. It was
a one-year M's program where you do the
coursework and the thesis concurrently.
And I said, I can defer my enrollment at
Claremont. So, if the Oxford degree
doesn't allow me to get better funding
or accepted into a better program or
something like that, I can just take up
my position at Claremont after the
degree at Oxford. And so, we went over
to Oxford. I did the program there. But
then that year, right as I was finishing
up my degree, I got an email from
Claremont saying that they were
restructuring their whole school, at
least their um programs related to
theology and religion, and so go find
something else to do. So now my backup
plan was no longer there, and I didn't
get accepted to uh any other PhD
programs. So I was actually uh left
without a program to attend for the
following year after finishing at
Oxford. And so I hurriedly emailed
Trinity Western University and said,
"Hey, hey, um could I possibly take up
that master's program that I was
accepted to last year and that I turned
down?" And fortunately for me, they said
sure. And then I was also able to get a
uh research assistantship that allowed
me to cover uh pretty much all of the
tuition. So I didn't do the second
master's degree because I was an
overachiever. I did it because my plans
fell through and I was left without a
program and I figured I needed to not
have any gaps in my graduate
uh career in order to be attractive to
PhD programs. And so I felt like I
needed to do that if I was going to
continue on in my graduate work. And so
when I talk about my second master's
degree, it's not because I had other
worlds I wanted to conquer and so wanted
to go do another graduate degree. It's
because I felt I was left really without
a choice. And the fit for this video has
been the flash.
